character.name: Ronin
character.location: On the road east of Hamilton
character.obligationNotes: Guilt: the community died after he refused the Institute. Bounty: the Institute may still hunt its disobedient infiltrator.
character.motivation: Honour without a master. Protect people whose lives are being treated as disposable. Discover whether a borrowed life can become his own.

talents.name: Jump Up
talents.notes: Once per round, stand as an incidental.

talents.name: Blade Technique
talents.notes: Use Agility for Melee checks. Damage still uses Strength.

talents.name: Parry
talents.notes: Suffer 3 strain per eligible melee hit to reduce damage by 4 before soak. Requires a Melee weapon.

talents.name: Quick Draw
talents.notes: Once per round, draw or holster an accessible item as an incidental.

inventory.name: Old community clothes and sandals
inventory.notes: Worn keepsakes. Worn on the road.

weapons.name: Street-sign katana
weapons.qualities: Hand-ground from a street-sign pole. Brawn + 2 damage; Blade Technique uses Agility for accuracy.

journal.title: A borrowed life
journal.body:
The Institute replaced a man in a community near Kansas City with an infiltrator synth who did not know what he was. The original man had no surviving family and was disliked; his replacement slowly found belonging among people whose culture had grown around a small surviving media collection, almost entirely Japanese samurai films. Kendo, communal honour and improvised Japanese-style blades shaped daily life.

When an Institute order unlocked his memories and commanded him to murder the elder and seize leadership, he refused. His community's values—and perhaps the knocks taken during training—had become more important than his programming. He warned the town. With retaliation already imminent, its people chose to fight beside him.

The Coursers were defeated. Ronin was the only person left standing. Expecting more hunters and with nobody left to remain for, he took his old clothes and the katana ground from a street-sign pole and walked away.

For a year he has survived alone. He calls himself Ronin: no master, no home, no settled identity. His easy smile and loose manner conceal grief and survivor's guilt. He cannot decide whether he destroyed his own life or a life he never had the right to claim. He helps strangers almost casually, then moves on before they can ask him to belong.

journal.title: A year heading west
journal.body: Over the past year, Ronin walked west from the Kansas City area through Robot City, Hangdogs territory, Black Canyon, Old Bones, Uintah, New Canaan, Eighties territory and Ruby Valley Refuge. He now approaches Hamilton in Riperult Territory, occasionally helping strangers and fighting raiders as he wanders.

character.notes: A year on the road. His old clothes and street-sign katana are all that remain of home. The easy smile hides a man still trying to decide which parts of his life belong to him.
